summary: Iter 11.1 backend-only regression PASS. Verified the 0.55 hardcoded confidence gate is removed from /api/scan-card (grep confirms no 'if conf_val < 0.55' remains in server.py; comment at line 459 states 'Confidence gate lives on the CLIENT'). All 3 identified=True return paths (strict, loose, no-price) echo the raw `confidence` field from the vision model. Full regression: 18/18 tests PASS via public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Pikachu Base 58 still identifies with name='Pikachu', language='english', price_source contains 'JustTCG', market price populated, low<=market<=high; history GET/DELETE clean (no _id leak); voice transcribe + chat (with/without context) OK; collection CRUD + summary grouping OK; /api/card/graded-prices returns 10-grade shape; /api/card/grade-estimate returns structured grades. New passthrough behavior verified: the blurry-image test now allows identified=true with any confidence value (previously required conf>=0.55 — that assertion is dead code with the gate removed). Test file updated accordingly; the change is a test-spec alignment, not a functional fix.

minor.issue: Heavily-degraded input images trigger long vision-model turnarounds (60–100s+) that occasionally exceed the Cloudflare edge timeout (~100s), yielding transient 502 Bad Gateway. Observed once on test_scan_blurry_low_quality; the retry succeeded. Not related to the iter 11.1 change. Consider adding a client-side pre-check (min image entropy / resolution) or a Gemini fast-fail branch so genuinely un-processable frames return quickly.

action_items: None required for iter 11.1. Change is minimal, tested, working. Client-side threshold is now authoritative as intended.

OPTIONAL: Guard against unprocessable images: if Gemini returns 'Unable to process input image' (BadRequestError 400), server should return a fast identified=false with reasoning='image unprocessable' instead of bubbling a 502 (currently /api/card/grade-estimate raises 502 on such payloads — visible in backend logs).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:459-460 comment cleanly documents the intent ('Confidence gate lives on the CLIENT'). No dead code left behind; the removed block is truly gone.

The response still passes ident.get('confidence') through on all three identified=True paths (strict, loose, no-price) and on both identified=false paths uses reasoning='No Pokemon card detected in frame' or 'Card visible but Pokemon name could not be read'. Client can now trust that identified=false is ONLY due to vision-model detection failure, never a threshold clamp.
No new deprecated Expo packages surfaced (no expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch).
